To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mouse-adpated scrapie strains, 139A and ME7, can be transmitted to the Golden hamsters, and generate 2 new hamsters-adapted strains.
the interspecies transmission can generate novel strains and the new strains can be stably maintained in the new host.

the mouse-adapated scrapie strains ME7 and 139A can be transmitted to hamsters to generate new hamster-adapated strains ME7-ha (or 139A-ham), and these strains have similar molecular and neuropathologic properties to their parent mouse strains, but have shorter incubation periods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transmission of prion diseases among species and provides a new insight into the molecular mechanism of prion diseases.
the transmission of prion diseases across species and the interspecies transmission and passage of prion diseases.

the interspecies transmission between mice and hamsters and the subsequent passaging in hamster, which may provide a new approach for the investigation on the molecular mechanisms underlying the interspecies transmission and the pathogenesis of prion disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 2 new scrapie agents, generated by interspecies transmission of ME7-mo and 139A-mo, have been successfully adapted to Golden hamster and can stably maintain their infectivity and molecular characteristics in this new host.
interspecies prion infection is not only a natural event, but also a useful tool for the generation of novel strains and the investigation of molecular properties of the new agents.
the interspecies infection of ME7-mo and 139A-mo into hamsters generated 2 new strains, ME7-mo-ha and 1st 139A-ho-ha, which can be further passaged and maintained in hamsters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mouse-adapting process of the scrapie agent is a dynamic and reversible process, and the interspecies barrier can be crossed by the scrapie agent in both directions.

the mouse-adaptive scrapie strains, which have been generated by serial passaging in mice, can be transmitted to hamsters to generate new hamster-adaptive strains, which are quite comparable with their mouse-adaptive parent strains in terms of incubation times, clinical courses and neuropathological changes.

the interspecies transmission from the original mouse host to the new host hamsters, followed by successive passage in the hamsters, can generate a novel strain that is more virulent and pathogenic than the original strain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the newly formed hamster scrapie strains can be used as a new animal model for the study of the molecular mechanism of interspecies transmission.
, in general, the incubation periods of the prion diseases are much shorter in the new host species than in the old host species.
the interspecies transmission may not be a rare event in nature.
